title: Sum-free sets
description: Sets of numbers in 1..n in which no two members (possibly the same one twice) add up to a third. Solver A guesses a set, solver C looks for a sum inside it, and the refinement says that one of the three numbers involved must leave the set.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Rules every solver needs. The constant n is set in the Loop tab.
num(1..n).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% Solver A proposes candidates: here, any set of numbers.
{ pick(X) : num(X) }.
#show pick/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The atoms solver A and solver C share. glue(T) makes T an interface atom:
% its value in a candidate is fixed when the check runs.
glue(pick(X)) :- num(X).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: every glue(T) makes T an interface atom.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% Solver C looks for a counterexample: a sum X + Y = Z inside the candidate.
1 { sum(X,Y) : num(X), num(Y), X <= Y, X + Y <= n } 1.
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(Y).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X+Y).
#show sum/2.

% relevant(T): the interface atoms the counterexample depends on.
% The refinement says: at least one of them must change.
relevant(pick(X)) :- sum(X,Y).
relevant(pick(Y)) :- sum(X,Y).
relevant(pick(X+Y)) :- sum(X,Y).
fragments.description: Looks for a counterexample to a candidate (solver C) and marks the atoms it depends on with relevant/1.

fragments.name: view
fragments.text:
% The numbers 1..n; picked numbers filled; the sum X + Y = Z of a counterexample ringed.
#program scene.
draw(layout(circle)).
draw(node(X)) :- num(X).

#program frame.
draw(attr(node(X), fill, picked)) :- cand(pick(X)).
draw(attr(node(X), stroke, sum)) :- cex(sum(X,_)).
draw(attr(node(Y), stroke, sum)) :- cex(sum(_,Y)).
draw(attr(node(X+Y), stroke, sum)) :- cex(sum(X,Y)).
draw(emph(node(X))) :- lit(pick(X), _).
draw(note("Picked numbers X, Y and X + Y: the ringed ones cannot all stay.")) :- kind(reject).
draw(note("No sum inside the picked set: a solution.")) :- kind(solution).
#show draw/1.
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
